text:
Pontus Holmberg was a sixth-round pick by Toronto in 2018 and a depth forward for most of his career. In Tampa Bay this season he's been a little more than that: 13 points in 17 games, nine in his last ten, including a four-point night against Winnipeg and two goals in the rematch.

The heater is mostly earned. His own chances are up to 1.21 expected goals per 60 from 0.89 last season, and he's playing only about 14 minutes a night, so his scoring rate per 60 is one of the best on the team. He's shooting 19.4%, which will come down, but the volume of good looks is real.

What made him valuable before was defense. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer chances with him on the ice than with almost any forward in the league, 99th percentile, and he draws more penalties than he takes. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him setting up teammates at the 91st percentile. Our range has him around 43 points, a career year. A promotion up the lineup would test whether this lasts.
headline: Pontus Holmberg is giving Tampa Bay more than expected
